thread:
maya: Heads-up: saw a 2.4x p95 regression on Mixtral-8B after applying the AWQ calibration set yesterday. Repro steps below and a short perf trace attached. :frowning:
alex_k: ugh, when did that land? CI shows the calibration commit merged ~08:12 UTC.
maya: right, commit 9f3b2d — calibration prompts updated + AWQ per-channel bias correction. Regression only shows up on long-seq (>=1024) runs.
benji: can you paste the exact repro command? also do we see differences between int8/awq/gptq runs?
maya: repro:
```
./run_infer --model mixtral-8b-awq-int8 --seq_len 1536 --batch 1 --prompt-file long_prompts.txt --profile=perf.data
perf record -o perf.data ./run_infer ...
```
maya: quick flame excerpt (perf report):
```
  34.1%  runtime  runtime  [kernel_select_generic_gemm]
  21.7%  runtime  runtime  [kv_cache_copy_overhead]
  12.4%  runtime  runtime  [rotary_rot_matmul_optimized]
```
elena_r: interesting — kernel selector prefers generic_gemm in the hot path. That would explain the token throughput drop.
benji: why would kernel selector pick generic_gemm for Mixtral? It should prefer the optimized rotary kernel unless RoPE params mismatch.
maya: exactly. I dumped the kernel selection log during the run, snippet:
```
[kernel_select] model=mixtral-8b variant=awq-int8 seq=1536 heads=32 kv_dim=128 rope_scale=0.99 -> selected=generic_gemm (fallback_reason=rope_scale_compat)
```
alex_k: rope_scale_compat? We added a conservative check in the selector last week to avoid numeric issues if rope_scale != 1.0
elena_r: but Mixtral's recommended RoPE scaling is 0.99 for long-context accuracy. That check is too coarse and forces non-optimized kernels.
benji: KV cache overhead is another signal — seems our KV packing path is doing small memcopies every token for seq>1024.
maya: KV cache trace (perf script):
```
kv_cache_write_page:  8k calls  120MB copied
kv_cache_frag_gc:    0.9% cpu
```
benji: oh, small page size + conservative append path results in fragmentation. For AWQ we saw smaller per-head kv elements (quantized pack size changed) which increased writes.
alex_k: hypothesis: AWQ calibration changed per-tensor packing alignment -> changed mm layout -> selector sees mismatch in expected rope stride -> selects generic_gemm -> latency spikes + extra memcopies for KV alignment.
elena_r: easy repro: run same model with rope_scale forced to 1.0 and see if selector picks optimized kernel.
maya: I tried that. With rope_scale=1.0 p95 back down to baseline. Changing packing alignment (pad to 64) also helped.
benji: good findings. Two tracks: (A) relax the rope_scale compatibility check with a tolerance window and add a warning, (B) make KV packing tolerant to smaller AWQ element layouts (pad at runtime).
alex_k: also add a quick unit test that runs selector on combos: (mixtral|mixtral-awq) x seq={128,512,1536} x rope_scale={0.99,1.0} expecting optimized kernel for known-good combos.
maya: will open a PR for (A) — quick fix to avoid fallback for 0.98..1.02 range. Adding logs so perf-bot can catch regressions.
perf-bot: [alert] kernel-selector: introduced new tolerance for rope_scale in 9f3b2d revert candidate created by @maya
elena_r: for (B) I'll prototype runtime padding for kv write to align to 64B blocks. That should remove the fragmentation.
benji: also let's add an eval check for AWQ calibration that measures throughput with a synthetic long-seq workload before merging.
alex_k: agree. CI should run a cheap long-seq perf sanity check for model onboarding. Put it in eng-runtime/perf-smoke.
maya: I'll revert the calibration commit on staging while we iterate, and add the perf unit. PRs: 4123 (rope_tolerance), 4124 (kv-pad), 4125 (longseq-ci). ETA EOD.
benji: thanks. assign me for validating packing changes on NV GPU farm.
alex_k: :thumbsup: keep notes here and paste flamegraphs or pprof links. If packing fix doesn't fully recover, we should consider kernel shim that supports both strides.
maya: extra note — calibration prompts included very short prompts which probably skewed quant stats. We'll re-run calibration with a balanced prompt mix after fixes.
elena_r: ack. I'll schedule a short sync tomorrow 10:30 to triage any follow-ups. :calendar:
maya: thanks all. will update thread with PR links and perf diffs.
